NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to implement a periodic low-current-density hold phase during cell operation to mitigate anode coating depletion. Standard practice operates the cell at constant current density; this intervention introduces a scheduled low-current-density period that reduces electrochemical dissolution of the RuO2/IrO2 coating. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is current-density throttling for process control, which is continuous and reactive; this intervention is a scheduled, proactive duty cycle that specifically targets coating dissolution kinetics. The mechanism exploits the inverse relationship between current density and anode dissolution rate, reducing cumulative coating loss per unit of chlorine produced.

PHYSICS CHECK — DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = anode dissolution rate; the mechanism moves it down by ~30-50% during hold phases by reducing current density from 3 kA/m² to 0.5 kA/m²; this reduces the electrochemical driving force for oxide dissolution. The dissolution rate follows the Tafel equation (i = i₀ exp(αηF/RT)), where reducing current density (i) directly lowers the dissolution rate (i₀ is the exchange current density, η is overpotential). At 0.5 kA/m², overpotential is reduced by ~200 mV, decreasing dissolution kinetics by an estimated factor of 3-5 during hold periods.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (standard practice: constant 3 kA/m² operation):
- (a) Existing cell power supply — reprogrammed duty cycle schedule
- (b) Standard process timer (commercial industrial timer, 24-hour programmable, DIN rail mount) — installed in control cabinet
- (c) Operating point change: set timer for 2-hour hold at 0.5 kA/m² every 24 hours
- (c) Operating point change: set power supply auto-ramp between normal and hold setpoints

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installation: 2 hours (timer installation vs. standard practice: 0 hours) — offset by eliminating recoating downtime (standard practice: 8 hours per campaign)
- Commissioning: 1 hour (timer programming vs. standard practice: 0 hours) — offset by reduced maintenance (standard practice: 2 hours per campaign for coating checks)
- Operational loss: Zero (hold periods scheduled during low-demand production windows)
- Maintenance: Same (no additional inspections; standard practice already monitors cell voltage)
- Cost class: Same (timer is standard catalog item; no new consumables)

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install timer and program duty cycle; run 1000-hour test with 10 identical cells (5 control, 5 intervention). Instruments: Existing cell voltage monitors and chlorine purity analyzers. Pass/fail: Intervention group shows <5% voltage rise at 1000 hours vs. >15% in control group, with O₂ in chlorine <0.1% in both. Kill criterion: >10% voltage rise in either group at 500 hours. Duration: 1000 hours (typical campaign length). Falsification: If intervention group voltage rise matches or exceeds control group, the mechanism fails.
